verdicts.reason: HELD, and it is the strongest claim in the packet. I opened both frames and cropped them myself. Nr4fQstqHDM_428.0.png: HP 20/20 green, 26/26 blue, third bar an EMPTY dark-brown track carrying grey 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE', '150% DAMAGE' in gold below. Nr4fQstqHDM_t435.0s.png, same portrait, same maxima (20 / 26), same 150% DAMAGE buff, HP now 19/20: the third bar is ~40% filled WHITE and carries NO text at all. Both HUD branches observed seven seconds apart in one run. The code matches verbatim: §1t113s0§.as:328 '(param1 - 48) / (param2 - 48)', clamp<0 at :329-332, :336-342 show the grey getString(960) label only at fill==0, :344-347 HIDE it while 0<fill<1, :348-359 swap to black getString(175) + Snd_criticalDamage at fill>=1. strings.json["175"]='Critical Hit'; '960' is genuinely absent from the 2,533-entry v0.682 table (I checked the key directly), and android BattleUI.updateReload (:259-263) has NO low-end label at all, only crittext gated on percentage>=1 — so the grey label is a web-v0.717 addition and the frame is what supplies its text. The mechanism is confirmed independently: §1t99s0§.as:3048-3051 '§1t4470s0§() { return this.§1t4469s0§() && this.§1t4414s0§ >= 48; }' and the stance cycler §1t4472s0§ at :3058-3063 returns early ONLY if reload < 48, then cycles stance. Its android twin is nextStance() at MCSPlayer.as:2975-2980, gated on 'reload < maxreload / 6' — a Focus gate on both builds, living on the BATTLE actor class. STANDING INVARIANT INVOKED: the measurement doc and the frame disagree and THE FRAME WINS — RR:178 recorded 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' at one instant and RR:158 turned that instant into 'HARD-LOCKED in v0.717'; the frame seven seconds later, same fight, shows the label gone and the bar filling. OVERTURN UPHELD IN FULL: RR:158-160 falls, and it falls harder than the finding says — not only is 'HARD-LOCKED' false, but RR:159-160's 'The recreation's Focus-gated in-combat switch models removed 2014 behavior' is false too, because a Focus-gated in-combat switch is exactly what v0.717 ships. RR:178's observation survives as an observation; only the inference drawn from it dies, which is what the finding itself says. One unstated precondition, minor: the label branch is additionally gated at :334 on '!§1t1540s0§.§1t9550s0§() && this.§1t5182s0§.visible', a mode check I did not resolve, so the HUD contract should carry it.

Every quoted line is verbatim. §1t99s0§.as:3272-3275 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ == this.§1t4415s0§) { return _loc2_ * 1.3 + this.§1t1243s0§; } return _loc2_;'. §1t5957s0§.as sets _loc42_ = 1.3 in ALL THREE stance branches (:2727 Light, :2736 Balanced, :2745 Heavy) and applies it at :2751 '_loc43_ = _loc1_ * _loc42_ + _loc12_'. :2746 '_loc47_ = 0.8' appears only in the Heavy branch (_loc47_ = 1 at :2728 and :2737), and the runtime twin is §1t99s0§.as:3286-3290 'if(this.stance == §1t12222s0§) { return defense * 0.8; } return defense;'. Both numbers are target-build source, so the promotion from wiki-sourced to CONTRACT is earned. OVERTURN UPHELD, but the finding names a slightly softer target than it should and I am recording the exact shape: the sentence quoted in ledger_text, 'Keep CRIT_MULT=1.3', is NOT made false — it is confirmed. What actually falls is (a) the parenthetical residual ask at RR:154, '(Read a real OG crit popup to fully seal it.)', which is discharged without any Ruffle session, (b) RR:88's KNOWN-UNKNOWNS entry 'crit ×1.3 vs ×3 final read', which the finding does name in lane_impact and which is now a KNOWN-KNOWN, and (c) RR:190 combat-core blocker ② 'crit 1.3 vs 3 final — read one crit popup', which closes. The rewrite must not say the 1.3 value was overturned; it was upgraded from wiki authority to web-source CONTRACT. Heavy-def 0.8 is likewise an evidence upgrade, not an overturn — RR:74 already carries it as a KNOWN-KNOWN, and the finding is honest about that. Minor defect: the text points the crit-proc caveat at 'RR:159 blocker ⑤' but RR:159 is the stance-lock paragraph; skills-meters blocker ⑤ lives at RR:195. And the caveat is itself over-cautious — see new finding N3, the proc rule IS settled.

The substance HELD on every artifact I opened. §1t1523s0§.as:2346 is verbatim 'var _loc2_:int = 90 + §1t7356s0§(§1t9426s0§) * 5;' and :2347 completes it as 'return int(120 + Math.floor(_loc2_ * param1 / (20 + param1)));'. :254 is 'internal static const §1t9426s0§:int = 25;' and android StatsManager.as:220 is 'internal static var STAT_DAN:int = 25;' with the plain-named twin at :1917. So dan rank does buy reach: maxincrement 90 at dan 0 -> 135 at dan 9, asymptote 210 px -> 255 px on top of the 120 px base. The ten titles are real and consecutive — I read strings.json["455"] through ["464"] one by one: (初段)(弐段)(参段)(四段)(五段)(六段)(七段)(八段)(九段)(十段), with ["465"]='Renshi' being a different thing, so the run really does end at 464. I also verified the cap the finding asserts, and I verified it on the WEB side rather than taking the android word for it: §1t1523s0§.as:2653 'if(§1t7356s0§(§1t9426s0§) < 9)' -> :2655 increments STAT_DAN, matching android StatsManager.as:2209-2211. Dan 0..9 = ten rungs = ten titles. OVERTURN UPHELD on RR:205 blocker ③ 'Dan-rank count/titles (garbled source)' — count and titles are both closed. MIS-CITE, recorded so the rewrite lands on the right line: the finding cites 'docs/research/REBUILD_READINESS.md:245' and its text says 'RR:245 blocker (3)'. RR:245 is the meta-social blocker list and its ③ is 'achievements list, daily-reward table, token costs'. The dan-rank blocker is RR:205 ③. The ledger_text field quotes the right sentence verbatim so the target is unambiguous, and citelint cannot catch this because 245 is a valid line — but the pointer is wrong by 40 lines and anyone applying the rewrite mechanically would gut the wrong blocker. Not fatal, because I re-derived the target from ledger_text and every artifact cite resolved. The finding also under-claims: it does not name RR:164-165 item 7, which this same evidence overturns (see new finding N5).

Verbatim on both builds. Web §1t401s0§.as:1954 'var _loc3_:int = §1t1525s0§.§1t9936s0§();' :1955-1958 clamp '>80 -> 80', :1959 'param1 = _loc3_ * 100;'. Materials branch on the SAME _loc3_: :1968 'if(_loc3_ < 30)' -> :1978 deducts 20061 by -2; :1980 'else if(_loc3_ < 60)' -> :1990-1991 deducts 20062 by -1 and 20063 by -2; :1993 'else' -> :2003-2005 deducts 20061 by -2, 20060 by -2, 20065 by -1. OVERTURN UPHELD: RR:80's 'Forge 700c+2 ore' is filed under '**Economy statics**' and it is not a static — it is min(nodeLevel,80)*100 with a three-tier material table, and 700c is just node level 7. RR:214's 'Ready: ... all service prices; Forge/Reinforce/Rebirth/Writ costs' and RR:216's Surface line 'Forge 700c' inherit the same error and must move with it. Two minor blemishes, neither factual about the game: the prose lists the five ore names in display order while the cite lists the ids in numeric order, so a careless reader pairs 20060 with Iron Ore instead of Coal; and it says 'Pairs with the reinforce finding already in this packet' when no reinforce finding is in this packet — I went and got it myself, see new finding N4.

Cleanest close in the packet. §1t401s0§.as:1058 is verbatim 'cost = §1t1525s0§.§1t9936s0§() * 10;' — and §1t9936s0§ is the SAME accessor the forge block calls at :1954, which is what ties it to node level rather than to character or weapon level. The menu copy at :662 is 'this.detailstext.text = §1t1521s0§.getString(848,[_loc1_ * 10]);' and I read strings.json["848"] directly: 'Repair your currently equipped weapon?\nCost: [0] coins' — so the currency is coins, from the game's own copy, not an assumption. Android InteractUI.as:1058 'cost = StageManager.getCurrentNodeLevel() * 10;' names the accessor in plain text, :647 is the matching getString(848,[level * 10]), and the semantics are settled at :1073-1076 'if(weapon.uses > 1) { weapon.uses = 1; }' — a durability reset, not a stat restore — refusing at :1066 on null weapon or itemID 0 or 13000, with the web guard at :1067-1068 identical. OVERTURN UPHELD: RR:215 economy blocker ③ 'Repair-Weapon cost (never captured)' is false; it is captured in one line of the target build, and the close-path note that it needs a preserved-build session goes with it. One of four named economy blockers closes.

Verbatim and the divergence is real. Web §1t1523s0§.as:2289-2296 is 'internal static function §1t9590s0§(param1:int) : Number { if(param1 > 600) { param1 = 600; } return 1 - param1 / 600 * 0.5; }'. Its feeder at :2279-2287 reads STAT_SPEED base plus gear bonus and multiplies by 1.5 while a buff flag is set, then calls it — so the input is effective SPD, exactly as claimed. Android StatsManager.as:1854-1860 is the same function with 300 in both places, and its feeder at :1844-1851 has the same 1.5 buff step. So SKILL_CD_MULT = 1 - min(SPD_eff, 600)/600 * 0.5 on web v0.717, floor 0.5x, versus a floor reached at 300 on android v0.682. This is a clean instance of the S0-3 parity caveat biting on COMBAT TUNING rather than UI copy, and the finding is right that a v0.717 recreation must take 600. OVERTURN UPHELD: RR:195 skills-meters blocker ④ 'SPD→cooldown formula' closes outright, RR:91's KNOWN-UNKNOWN 'the SPEED-stat→cooldown formula' leaves that list, and the cooldown half of RR:200 progression blocker ① falls. The finding correctly leaves the DEF-mitigation half of RR:200 ① standing — I found nothing that touches it. It under-claims on one point: RR:200 ① also says 'SPD **range**', and that half falls too, from the sibling function twelve lines below the one this finding read. See new finding N1.

The contract HELD, and I verified the obfuscation mapping myself rather than trusting the pairing. §1t99s0§.as:183-199 and MCSPlayer.as:182-198 are the same fifteen-parameter init in the same order, which fixes §1t4413s0§=maxchi, §1t4419s0§=baseReload, §1t4420s0§=baseSlashLength, §1t4421-4423s0§=light/balanced/heavy mastery; and §1t4478s0§/§1t4479s0§ are line-for-line deductReloadBar()/bonusReload(), which is what proves §1t4414s0§=reload and §1t4415s0§=maxreload. CAPACITY: §1t1523s0§.as:2276 'return 48 + (§1t7356s0§(§1t9410s0§) + §1t7358s0§(§1t9410s0§)) * 6;' = android :1841, so max = 48 + (SPD + gear SPD) * 6 and 48 is the meter's floor — which is why the HUD zero point and the stance gate are both literally 48. CONSUMPTION: :3295-3297 zeroes a full meter first, then :3299-3311 subtract slashUsage/2 (Light), slashUsage (Balanced and 12224), slashUsage*1.5 (Heavy and 12223), clamped at 0 by :3312-3315; slashUsage floors at 48 per android StatsManager.as:1921-1929. REGEN: :3320 '+= 6', clamped, then pushed to the HUD updater §1t113s0§.§1t5205s0§ at :3325 — which is the direct link proving the frame's third bar IS this meter, and it is the joint that makes the stance finding and this one one system. OVERTURN UPHELD: RR:195 blocker ③ 'Focus numerics (max/fill/switch-cost)' closes, RR:190 blocker ⑤ 'Focus/crit gating rule' closes, and RR:89's KNOWN-UNKNOWN 'the Focus/crit gating rule (fill trigger/amount/consumption)' leaves that list. MATERIAL DEFECT IN lane_impact, not in the claim text: lane_impact says 'regen +6/tick'. The text says '+6 per call', which is honest, but the call site was never opened. I opened it. bonusReload() has exactly ONE caller in the android bundle — NPCManager.as:1709-1711 'if(deathCount > 0) { StatsManager.getPlayer().bonusReload(); }', inside the per-frame die-check sweep. Focus regen is ON KILL, not a per-tick trickle. Shipping '+6/tick' would produce a meter that fills while the player stands still, which is a different game. The contract survives with that one field corrected — see new finding N2.

new_findings.text: RR:190 combat-core blocker ① calls the per-stance reach cap 'the one value the whole model needs' and says the wiki gives 'units of unknown scale'. It is fully specified in web v0.717 source, in STAGE PIXELS, and nobody in this packet claimed it — two findings walked past it. BASE: §1t1523s0§.as:2334-2341 computes SPD_eff = STAT_SPEED + gear SPD, x1.5 while the speed buff is set, and passes it to :2344-2348, which returns 120 + floor((90 + DAN*5) * SPD_eff / (20 + SPD_eff)). The unit question is answered by the game's own UI: the stats panel prints int(baseSlashLength * slashModifier) as 'slash distance' — android InventoryUI.as:2232 in plain names, web §1t5957s0§.as:3013 with _loc21_ = §1t9593s0§(...) and _loc48_ the same three multipliers — so the number IS the drawn blade-path length. new_findings.build: android v0.682 supplies the call site; web v0.717 supplies the identical body
new_findings.text: The Focus finding in this packet ships 'regen +6/tick' in its lane_impact. That trigger was never opened, and it is wrong. bonusReload() has exactly one caller in the whole android bundle: NPCManager.as:1709-1711, inside the sweep at :1695-1706 that walks the enemy list, calls checkDie() on each, and counts deaths — so the +6 fires once per frame in which at least one enemy DIED, not once per frame. Focus is a kill-fed resource. That is also why the frames make sense: at Nr4fQstqHDM_428.0 the bar sits at zero mid-fight, and by t435.0s, after kills, it is ~40% full. A per-tick trickle would never sit empty through an active fight. Note the build divergence in the same function while I was there: android :3272 pushes '(this.reload - 24) / (this.maxreload - 24)' to the HUD, while web §1t113s0§.as:328 computes '(param1 - 48) / (param2 - 48)' inside the HUD from raw values — so the bar's zero point is 24 on android and 48 on web. Only on WEB does the empty bar coincide exactly with the stance gate at 48, which is precisely why the web build can afford to use the empty bar as the 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' readout and android carries no such label.
new_findings.lane_impact: L2 skills-meters / L5 combat-core: corrects the Focus contract before it ships. FOCUS_REGEN = +6 per kill event (clamped to max), NOT per tick. Do not write '+6/tick' into config. Also record the web/android HUD zero-point divergence (48 vs 24) so the third bar is not ported from the android formula.

new_findings.text: RR:195 skills-meters blocker ⑤ says the crit PROC rule is 'entirely absent' and asks whether it is chance or deterministic, and the crit finding in this packet declines to settle it, saying :3272 'tests an equality between two obfuscated members, not a probability'. The members are not unknown. The fifteen-parameter init at §1t99s0§.as:183-199 maps one-for-one onto android MCSPlayer.as:182-198, and §1t4478s0§/§1t4479s0§ are line-for-line deductReloadBar()/bonusReload() — android :3242-3244 'if(this.reload == this.maxreload) { this.reload = 0; }' is the same statement as web :3295-3297 with plain names. So §1t4414s0§ = reload and §1t4415s0§ = maxreload, and :3272 reads 'if the Focus meter is FULL'. Crit is DETERMINISTIC: a full meter guarantees x1.3 on the next hit, and the same full meter is zeroed by the spend that follows, so exactly one crit per fill. There is no probability anywhere in the path — Math.random() appears at :3281 for the damage RANGE roll and nowhere in the crit branch. The HUD agrees and is visible to the player: §1t113s0§.as:348-359 shows black 'Critical Hit' plus Snd_criticalDamage the moment fill >= 1, i.e. the game TELLS you the crit is armed, which only makes sense for a deterministic rule.
new_findings.ledger_text: ⑤ crit **proc** rule (chance vs deterministic) — entirely absent.
new_findings.lane_impact: L2 skills-meters blocker ⑤ CLOSES as CONTRACT, and it is the one this packet's crit finding explicitly left open. CRIT_PROC = deterministic on reload == maxreload, consumed by the same hit. Combined with the Focus finding this makes crit a resource the player spends, not a dice roll — which changes the combat model, not just a number.

new_findings.text: The forge finding in this packet says it 'pairs with the reinforce finding already in this packet'. There is no reinforce finding in this packet, so I went and read it. The result is a HALF-correction to the same ledger line, and it is different in shape from the forge one, which is why it must not be assumed. The COIN cost genuinely IS a static — InteractUI.as:1083 'cost = 5000;' with no formula, and all three display strings hard-code 'Cost: 5000 coins'. The MATERIAL is not: it branches on the equipped WEAPON's level, not the node level, at :1097-1131 — below 30 costs 1x 20064, below 60 costs 1x 20065, otherwise 1x 20066, with a special case at :1098-1101 forcing itemID 13022 to weaponlevel 59. I resolved the ids: 20064 Silver Ore, 20065 Titanium Ore, 20066 Uncut Diamond, matching strings.json["850"]/["851"]/["852"] exactly. The effect is settled at :1133 'weapon.uses = 0;' — unbreakable, which is what the copy promises. So RR:80's 'Reinforce 5000c+1 silver ore' carries the lowest of three material tiers and presents it as the whole rule, the same defect the forge finding identifies, but the price half of RR:80 survives here where it did not for forge. PARITY CAVEAT, stated because it is undischarged: I could not confirm the 5000 on the web side, so this row is v0.682 under S0-3.

new_findings.text: S0-3's parity caveat says UI copy and combat tuning parity between web v0.717 and android v0.682 is NOT established. Judging this packet measured four concrete divergences, all in COMBAT TUNING rather than copy, which discharges the caveat's 'not established' into 'established, and they differ'. (1) SPD->cooldown cap: 600 on web, 300 on android — the mobile build halves cooldowns at half the stat. (2) In-combat stance gate: a flat 'reload < 48' on web, 'reload < maxreload / 6' on android — which is 8 + SPD, so the two only agree at SPD 40. (3) HUD reload zero point: 48 on web, 24 on android; only the web build's empty bar coincides with its stance gate, which is why only the web build can use the empty bar as the 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' readout and android's BattleUI carries no such label. (4) Per-stance reach multipliers: web 1.4 / 1 + 0.02m / 0.5 + 0.04m against android 1.5 / 1 + 0.005M / 0.5 + 0.005M. In every one of the four the web value is the one a v0.717 recreation must take, and in every one an agent porting the android row would have shipped a wrong number that no test would catch. Corollary for this lane's own rules: a claim resting on an android combat constant while asserting web behaviour is not a theoretical parity hole — it is wrong four times out of four in the region I sampled.
